page: Amazon Web Services r6g.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an ARM64-based AWS Graviton2 processor utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it operates on a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities alongside weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth results. The stress-ng single-core CPU test yielded an average score of 1519.48, while the multi-core CPU test scored 3014.98, placing it in the lower tier of multi-core performance. Memory bandwidth tests show 36.62 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 18.28 GB/sec for large block write operations. Geekbench scores reflect lower-tier performance, with a single-core score of 933.0 and a multi-core score of 1706.0. Database operations under Passmark scored 1309.06, and Redis SET operations achieved 2.28 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r6g.large leverages the ARM64 architecture to provide a high memory footprint relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive CPU performance. The absence of local storage means storage requirements must be met via network-attached options. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive applications with moderate compute needs, such as caching layers, small database deployments, and lightweight web serving.
